answer: An identity may act only when the inlet admits its cedar board, and the inlet admits a board only if it carries a burn mark for every head its root has ever filed, each mark cut by a grove that has never burned for that root, the char carrying that grove's signature. Each grove takes one measure of shale for the burn, forfeit if the head proves false. An honest newcomer buys one grove and one measure; a root's thousandth clone needs a thousand fresh groves and a thousand measures, each won on its own, and its owner has burned half a million.
